title: Constant Coefficients: Distinct Real Roots
short: Try y = e^(rt) and solve the characteristic equation.

blocks.html: For constant coefficients, $ay'' + by' + cy = 0$, the derivatives of the unknown must cancel against the function itself. Exponentials are the functions whose derivatives are multiples of themselves, so we try $y = e^{rt}$, exactly as in checking a solution and in superposition.
Substituting $y = e^{rt}$ gives the characteristic equation $$ar^{2} + br + c = 0.$$ If it has two distinct real roots $r_1 \ne r_2$, the general solution is $y = c_1e^{r_1t} + c_2e^{r_2t}$.

With $y = e^{rt}$: $y' = re^{rt}$ and $y'' = r^{2}e^{rt}$, so $ay'' + by' + cy$ $= (ar^{2} + br + c)e^{rt}$. Since $e^{rt} \ne 0$, this is zero exactly when $r$ solves the characteristic equation. Two different roots give two solutions with $W = (r_2 - r_1)e^{(r_1 + r_2)t} \ne 0$, so they are independent and superposition gives every solution.

blocks.title: A zero root
steps: $r^{2} + 3r = r(r + 3) = 0$: $r = 0, -3$. The root 0 gives the constant solution $e^{0t} = 1$.

blocks.html: Reading the roots with the wrong sign: $(r - 2)(r + 3) = 0$ means $r = 2$ and $r = -3$, so the solutions are $e^{2t}$ and $e^{-3t}$. A quick check: substitute one exponential back; $4 + 2 - 6 = 0$ confirms $r = 2$. Also keep both constants: $e^{2t} + e^{-3t}$ alone cannot match two arbitrary initial values.

blocks.name: graph
blocks.cap: The solution $2e^{2t} - e^{-3t}$ (solid) is the sum of its two exponential parts (dashed). For large $t$ the growing term $e^{2t}$ dominates; for negative $t$ the other one does.
